zh_CN: 手术部女更衣室的门轻轻合上。朝仓美幸将白色护士服挂进柜子，把一套浅绿色刷手服放在长凳上。
en: The door to the surgical department's women's changing room closed softly. Miyuki Asakura hung her white nurse's uniform in a locker and placed a set of light green scrubs on the bench.

zh_CN: 「呼……今天居然让我跟这么长的手术。实习评价里也会写这一项吧？」
en: “Phew… They’re actually letting me assist with such a long operation today. This will go on my internship evaluation too, right?”

zh_CN: 「紧张？」
en: “Nervous?”

zh_CN: 「前辈以前跟过这样的长台吧？我昨天把流程背了一遍，还是有点没底。」
en: “You’ve assisted with long cases like this before, haven’t you? I memorized the procedure yesterday, but I still feel unsure.”

zh_CN: 「嗯？跟过呀。」
en: “Hmm? Of course.”

zh_CN: 「太好了！那我今天一定好好跟着您学！」
en: “Wonderful! Then I’ll make sure to learn everything I can from you today!”

zh_CN: 「呵呵。这句话先记着，等你看到器械台再说一次。」
en: “Hehe. Remember that. Say it again when you see the instrument table.”

zh_CN: 「诶？为什么？」
en: “Huh? Why?”

zh_CN: 「因为那个时候，我会请你先把注意力放在自己的工作上。」
en: “Because then I'll ask you to concentrate on your own work first.”

zh_CN: 朝仓将腕表和随身饰物收好，动作熟练地整理柜内衣物。年轻护士则拿着刷手裤，仍在研究腰间的系带。
en: Asakura put away her watch and accessories, deftly arranging her belongings in the locker. The younger nurse held a pair of scrub trousers, still studying the ties at the waist.

zh_CN: 「这种裤子原来是系带的呀。我还以为会像病房制服一样有拉链。」
en: “Oh, these trousers tie shut. I thought they'd have a zipper like our ward uniforms.”

zh_CN: 「你从病房过来，第一天不习惯很正常。」
en: “You've come from the ward. It's normal to find things unfamiliar on your first day.”

zh_CN: 朝仓将私人衣物连同内衣一起收进柜中，直接换上刷手裤和上衣，随后抻平袖口。
en: Asakura put her personal clothes, including her underwear, into the locker, changed straight into the scrub trousers and top, then smoothed her sleeves.

zh_CN: 「怎么了？」
en: “What is it?”

zh_CN: 「前、前辈……里面也要全部换掉吗？」
en: “Um... Do we have to change everything underneath too?”

zh_CN: 「我们手术部上台时一直是这个习惯呀。」
en: “That's how we've always dressed for operations in our surgical department.”

zh_CN: 「我以为直接把刷手服套在自己的内衣外面就可以了……」
en: “I thought I could just put the scrubs on over my own underwear...”

zh_CN: 「可以理解。病房里可不会有人特地教你怎么换手术服。」
en: “Understandable. Nobody on the ward specifically teaches you how to change for the operating room.”

zh_CN: 「那……为什么要这样？大家都是这么穿的吗？」
en: “Then... why? Does everyone dress like that?”

zh_CN: 「至少我们这里上长台的时候，大家都尽量不把自己的贴身衣物带进去。弄湿了很麻烦的。」
en: “At least here, we try not to wear our own undergarments during long operations. It's a nuisance if they get wet.”

zh_CN: 「弄湿？您是说汗吗？」
en: “Wet? You mean from sweat?”

zh_CN: 「汗也有。还有冲洗液、血液……运气不好，隔着刷手服也不一定能幸免。」
en: “That too. Irrigation fluid, blood... If you're unlucky, even your scrubs won't keep it all out.”

zh_CN: 「血、血会弄到自己内衣上？！实习手册里可没写这条！」
en: “B-blood can get on our underwear?! That wasn’t in the internship handbook!”

zh_CN: 年轻护士下意识地低头看了看自己的衣服。朝仓看着她突然僵住的表情，嘴角微微翘了起来。
en: The younger nurse instinctively glanced down at her clothes. Watching her suddenly stiffen, Asakura's lips curled slightly upward.

zh_CN: 「呵呵，有什么奇怪的？我们是在做手术，又不是小孩子过家家。」
en: “Hehe, what's so strange? We're performing surgery, not playing house.”

zh_CN: 「我知道是在做手术！可我还以为……那个……」
en: “I know it's surgery! But I thought... well...”

zh_CN: 「以为血液都会乖乖待在患者身上，等我们处理完再消失？」
en: “You thought all the blood would stay obediently inside the patient and disappear once we were done?”

zh_CN: 「前辈……您是不是故意吓实习生呀！」
en: “Are you… trying to scare the intern on purpose!”

zh_CN: 「可我说的是真话呀。」
en: “But I'm telling the truth.”

zh_CN: 朝仓眨眨眼，笑容甜得让人找不到可以抱怨的地方。
en: Asakura blinked, her smile so sweet it left little room for complaint.

zh_CN: 「你那条可爱的粉红色小裤子，要是沾上女患者的血，回家不是很难办吗？」
en: “If those cute pink panties of yours get a female patient's blood on them, won't that be awkward when you get home?”

zh_CN: 「为、为什么连颜色都看到了？！」
en: “H-how did you even see the color?!”

zh_CN: 「刚才你换下病房护士裙的时候，我刚好瞥见了一眼呀。我只是替它担心嘛。」
en: “I happened to catch a glimpse when you took off your ward uniform just now. I'm only worrying about them.”

zh_CN: 「呜……您真的在取笑我……」
en: “Ooh… You really are making fun of me…”

zh_CN: 「才没有呢。你想想，换洗医院的衣服容易，弄脏自己喜欢的内衣就不划算了。」
en: “I'm not. Think about it. Hospital clothes are easy to get washed. Ruining underwear you like isn't worth it.”

zh_CN: 「……好，我现在就换。今天我可不想在这种地方出岔子。」
en: “…All right, I’ll change now. I don’t want to slip up over something like this today.”

zh_CN: 「放心。大部分时候只要做好防护，就不会有什么事。只是长台上的意外，最好在进去之前想清楚。」
en: “Don't worry. Most of the time, proper protection keeps everything fine. It's just best to consider what might happen during a long operation before going in.”

zh_CN: 「为什么这句安慰您不早点说啊……」
en: “Why didn't you say the reassuring part first...?”

zh_CN: 「你刚才那个表情太有趣了，我一不小心就讲多了。」
en: “Your expression was so amusing that I got a little carried away.”

zh_CN: 年轻护士将自己的贴身衣物收入柜中，重新穿好刷手裤和上衣。她走了两步，又停下来，悄悄拉了拉裤子的布料。
en: The younger nurse put her undergarments in the locker and dressed properly in her scrub trousers and top. She took a few steps, stopped, and discreetly tugged at the fabric of her trousers.

zh_CN: 「怎么？这次又发现什么了？」
en: “What is it? Found something else this time?”

zh_CN: 「裤子……直接贴着皮肤，走起来有一点磨。」
en: “The trousers... They rub a little when I walk, directly against my skin.”
“Mm.”

zh_CN: 「上衣也是。不穿胸罩的话，胸前碰到布料，感觉好粗糙……」
en: “The top too. Without a bra, the fabric against my chest feels so rough...”

zh_CN: 「我还以为是自己适应能力太差……前辈真的一点都不在意吗？」
en: “I thought I was just terrible at adapting… Does it really not bother you at all?”

zh_CN: 「我第一次穿这种料子的时候，也觉得硬。」
en: “The first time I wore this fabric, I thought it was stiff too.”

zh_CN: 「咦？前辈也会这样？」
en: “Huh? You did too?”

zh_CN: 「当然会呀。我又不是用刷手服的布做出来的。」

zh_CN: 「我还以为习惯了以后，就连这些感觉都不会有呢。」

zh_CN: 「听起来又有点可怕了……」

zh_CN: 「但是这批衣服确实硬了点。让我看看。」

zh_CN: 「可以换吗？」

zh_CN: 「能换为什么不换？今天你要站好几个小时，又不是来练习忍耐比赛的。」

zh_CN: 「回头我跟院长提一句。下一批至少换种舒服点的布料。」

zh_CN: 「很好。那就先去看看我们今天到底是不是在过家家吧。」

en: “I thought once you got used to it, you wouldn't even notice those things anymore.”

zh_CN: 「忙起来就忘了。尤其医生突然伸手要器械的时候，你哪还有空想裤子磨不磨。」
en: “You forget when you're busy. Especially when the doctor suddenly holds out a hand for an instrument. Who has time to think about their trousers chafing then?”

zh_CN: 「听起来又有点可怕了……」
en: “That sounds a little frightening again...”

zh_CN: 「但是这批衣服确实硬了点。让我看看。」
en: “But this batch really is a bit stiff. Let me see.”

zh_CN: 朝仓捏起自己的袖口，和年轻护士上衣的布料对了对，又翻看了一眼衣领内侧。
en: Asakura pinched her own sleeve and compared its fabric with the younger nurse's top, then checked inside the collar.

zh_CN: 「嗯，应该是新送来那批。洗过的旧衣服反而柔软些。」
en: “Mm, these must be from the new delivery. Older ones that have been washed are actually softer.”

zh_CN: 「所以不是我太奇怪？」
en: “So it's not just me being strange?”

zh_CN: 「当然不是。衣服不合适就是不合适，靠忍着又不会让它变软。」
en: “Of course not. Uncomfortable clothes are uncomfortable. Putting up with them won't make them softer.”

zh_CN: 「隔壁柜子有洗软的备用服。我给你拿一套，尺寸应该合适。」
en: “There are some spare sets that have softened in the wash in the next locker. I'll get you one. It should be your size.”

zh_CN: 「可以换吗？」
en: “Am I allowed to change?”

zh_CN: 「能换为什么不换？今天你要站好几个小时，又不是来练习忍耐比赛的。」
en: “Why wouldn't you, if you can? You'll be standing for hours today. You're not here for an endurance contest.”

zh_CN: 朝仓从备用柜中取出一套折好的刷手服递给她，自己顺手把偏硬的新衣服叠好放到待检查的一边。
en: Asakura took a folded set of scrubs from the spare locker and handed it over, then folded the stiff new set and put it aside to be checked.

zh_CN: 「回头我跟院长提一句。下一批至少换种舒服点的布料。」
en: “I'll mention it to the director later. At least we can get more comfortable fabric next time.”

zh_CN: 「前辈，您连哪一批衣服有毛病都知道啊？」
en: “You even know which batch of clothes has problems?”

zh_CN: 「穿着不舒服，还要穿一整天，当然得管。我们又不是只有患者要照顾。」
en: “If we have to wear something uncomfortable all day, of course I do. Patients aren't the only people we need to look after.”

zh_CN: 「……明明刚才还那么坏心眼。」
en: “...And you were being so mean just a moment ago.”

zh_CN: 「嗯？刚才怎么了？」
en: “Hmm? What happened a moment ago?”

zh_CN: 「您真的要装作不知道吗！」
en: “Are you really going to pretend you don't know?!”

zh_CN: 年轻护士终于笑了出来。两人先后拿起手术帽戴上。朝仓帮她把备用服的领口整理平整，又检查了一遍还没完全压好的帽沿。
en: The younger nurse finally laughed. They each picked up a surgical cap and put it on. Asakura straightened the collar of the spare scrub top for her, then checked the cap's rim, which was not quite tucked into place yet.

zh_CN: 「前辈，您平时还说自己在星见算新人。听着可一点都不像。」
en: “You’re always saying you count as a newcomer at Hoshimi. You certainly don’t sound like one.”

zh_CN: 「是呀。」
en: “That's right.”

zh_CN: 「可您连哪一批刷手服的料子不好都知道。刚才提到长台，也像做过很多次一样。」
en: “But you even know which batch of scrubs has bad fabric. And when you mentioned long operations, you sounded like you'd done lots of them.”

zh_CN: 「我说的是在星见没经验，又不是今天才学会当护士。」
en: “I said I was inexperienced at Hoshimi, not that I learned to be a nurse today.”

zh_CN: 「还有，你那边的手术帽压好。耳朵和发尾都别留在外面。」
en: “And tuck that side of your cap in properly. Keep your ears and the ends of your hair inside.”

zh_CN: 「是！前辈！」
en: “Yes! I will!”

zh_CN: 朝仓戴好口罩，拉开通往手术部走廊的门。年轻护士快步跟上，脸上的紧张仍在，脚步却比进更衣室时稳了许多。
en: Asakura put on her mask and opened the door to the surgical corridor. The younger nurse hurried after her. Her face was still nervous, but her steps were much steadier than when she had entered the changing room.

zh_CN: 「前辈，要是我真的在台边紧张起来，您会提醒我的吧？」
en: “If I really do get nervous at the table, you’ll give me a reminder, won’t you?”

zh_CN: 「先看我在做什么。听不懂就问，没把握就说。这个比假装镇定有用多了。」
en: “First, watch what I'm doing. Ask if you don't understand. Say so if you're unsure. That's much more useful than pretending to be calm.”

zh_CN: 「明白了。」
en: “Understood.”

zh_CN: 「很好。那就先去看看我们今天到底是不是在过家家吧。」
en: “Good. Then let's go see whether we really are playing house today.”

zh_CN: 「前辈！您就是故意的啦！」
en: “You’re doing that on purpose!”

zh_CN: 两人的声音沿着手术部走廊渐渐远去。
en: Their voices gradually faded down the surgical corridor.

zh_CN: 周日的约会广场比平日热闹得多。坂口在长椅上翻过手机屏幕，抬头又看了一眼来往的人群。
en: The plaza is much busier on Sunday than on weekdays. Sakaguchi turns his phone over on the bench and looks up once more at the people passing by.

zh_CN: 他和朝仓美幸约的是下午两点。现在，广场时钟的分针已经慢悠悠地走过了下一圈。
en: He and Miyuki Asakura agreed to meet at two in the afternoon. Now the minute hand on the plaza clock has leisurely completed another lap.

zh_CN: 「……她不会出了什么事吧。」
en: “…I hope nothing’s happened to her.”

zh_CN: 坂口再次拨号。铃声响了很久，才终于有人接听。
en: Sakaguchi calls again. The phone rings for a long time before someone finally answers.
“…Hello?”

zh_CN: 「朝仓？你现在在哪儿？」
en: “Asakura? Where are you now?”

zh_CN: 「……嗯……坂口医生？」
en: “…Mm… Dr. Sakaguchi?”

zh_CN: 「对，是我。你没事吧？」
en: “Yes, it’s me. Are you all right?”

zh_CN: 电话那头传来一阵窸窸窣窣的声音。接着是有什么东西掉到地板上的闷响。
en: Rustling comes through the phone, followed by the dull thud of something falling onto the floor.
“Aaah—!!!”

zh_CN: 「怎么了？！」
en: “What happened?!”

zh_CN: 「糟了！！我睡过头了！！」
en: “Oh no!! I overslept!!”
“…Overslept?”

zh_CN: 「今天是不是星期天？！我们是不是约了两点？！」
en: “Is today Sunday?! Were we supposed to meet at two?!”

zh_CN: 「是。现在三点十分。」
en: “Yes. It’s ten past three now.”
“Th-three?!”

zh_CN: 电话那头突然安静了两秒，随后响起急促的脚步声。
en: The other end falls silent for two seconds, then hurried footsteps follow.

zh_CN: 「你还在等我吗？！」
en: “Are you still waiting for me?!”

zh_CN: 「还在。」
en: “I am.”

zh_CN: 「对不起！真的对不起！我马上就来！」
en: “I’m sorry! I’m so sorry! I’ll be right there!”

zh_CN: 「先别急。你昨晚值班了吗？」
en: “Don’t rush. Were you on duty last night?”

zh_CN: 「没有呀。」
en: “No.”

zh_CN: 「那怎么睡到现在？」
en: “Then how did you sleep until now?”

zh_CN: 「因为昨天那部电视剧！最后一集停在那么过分的地方，怎么可能不继续看嘛！」
en: “It’s that drama I watched yesterday! The last episode ended on such an outrageous cliffhanger. How could I possibly stop there!”

zh_CN: 「……所以你看了一整夜？」
en: “…So you watched all night?”

zh_CN: 「看到天亮了，后来想稍微睡一下……一睁眼就听到你的电话了。」
en: “Until sunrise. Then I thought I’d sleep for a little while… The next thing I knew, your call woke me.”

zh_CN: 「真的是『稍微』啊。」
en: “Quite a ‘little while.’”

zh_CN: 「不许笑！我二十分钟……不，三十分钟就到！」
en: “Don’t laugh! I’ll be there in twenty… no, thirty minutes!”

zh_CN: 「慢慢来。把鞋穿对就好。」
en: “Take your time. Just make sure you put your shoes on properly.”

zh_CN: 「坂口医生！！」
en: “Dr. Sakaguchi!!”

zh_CN: 电话挂断。坂口看着已经暗下来的屏幕，又抬头看了看下午三点的天空。
en: The call ends. Sakaguchi looks at the dark screen, then up at the three-o’clock afternoon sky.

zh_CN: 「……医院里那个连交班提前五分钟都能发现的朝仓，居然……」
en: “…Asakura notices even a handover five minutes early at the hospital, and yet…”

zh_CN: 四十分钟后，朝仓从广场另一端小跑过来。她穿着轻巧的私服，肩上挎着小包，发梢还带着匆忙整理过的弧度。
en: Forty minutes later, Asakura jogs over from the far side of the plaza. She is in light casual clothes with a small bag over her shoulder, her hair still showing the curves of a hurried styling.

zh_CN: 「坂口医生——！」
en: “Dr. Sakaguchi—!”

zh_CN: 「你终于来了。」
en: “You finally made it.”

zh_CN: 「对不起嘛……」
en: “I’m sorry…”

zh_CN: 她双手合十，笑得又乖又甜。坂口刚想开口，朝仓便自己先举起手机。
en: She presses her palms together, smiling sweetly and obediently. Before Sakaguchi can speak, Asakura raises her phone.

zh_CN: 「我保证，闹钟真的有设。」
en: “I promise, I really did set an alarm.”

zh_CN: 「设在几点？」
en: “For what time?”
“…Eleven.”

zh_CN: 「那为什么三点才醒？」
en: “Then why did you only wake up at three?”

zh_CN: 「我也很想知道呀。手机显示我把它按掉了，可我完全不记得。」
en: “I’d like to know too. My phone says I turned it off, but I don’t remember doing it at all.”

zh_CN: 「你把医院的排班表记得那么清楚，却记不住自己按过闹钟？」
en: “You remember the hospital rota so clearly, but not turning off your own alarm?”

zh_CN: 「那可不一样。医院有患者等着，当然不能乱来。」
en: “That’s different. Patients are waiting at the hospital. Of course I can’t be careless.”

zh_CN: 「休息日的话……稍微赖个床，又不会有人需要开刀。」
en: “On a day off… nobody needs surgery just because I stay in bed a little longer.”

zh_CN: 「今天有人等了你一个多小时。」
en: “Someone waited for you for over an hour today.”

zh_CN: 「呜……这个我认错。请问坂口医生，要怎样才肯原谅我呢？」
en: “Ooh… I admit that was my fault. What would it take for you to forgive me, Dr. Sakaguchi?”

zh_CN: 「至少先去吃点东西吧。我都快饿了。」
en: “Let’s at least get something to eat first. I’m getting hungry.”

zh_CN: 「好！今天我请客。你想吃什么都可以！」
en: “All right! My treat today. You can have anything you like!”

zh_CN: 「真的？」
en: “Really?”

zh_CN: 「嗯……除了那种要预约三个月的高级餐厅。」
en: “Well… except the kind of fancy restaurant you have to book three months ahead.”

zh_CN: 「条件还挺多。」
en: “Quite a few conditions attached.”

zh_CN: 「因为我连早饭都还没吃呢。先救救我嘛。」
en: “I haven’t even had breakfast yet. Have mercy on me first.”

zh_CN: 她轻轻扯住坂口的袖口，朝商店街走去。刚才的窘迫没有持续多久，步伐已经重新变得轻快。
en: She gently tugs Sakaguchi’s sleeve and heads toward the shopping street. Her embarrassment doesn’t last long; there is already a spring in her step again.

zh_CN: 两人走进一家还供应下午茶的小餐厅。窗边的座位能看见街上的行人，桌上摆着印着花纹的纸菜单。
en: They enter a small restaurant still serving afternoon tea. Their window seat overlooks the pedestrians outside, and patterned paper menus lie on the table.

zh_CN: 「咦……午餐套餐已经结束了。」
en: “Huh… They’ve stopped serving the lunch set.”

zh_CN: 「现在快四点了。」
en: “It’s almost four.”

zh_CN: 「我知道啦。可是我今天还没吃午餐呀。」
en: “I know. But I haven’t had lunch today.”

zh_CN: 「所以你的午餐时间跟医院完全不一样。」
en: “So your lunchtime is nothing like the hospital’s.”

zh_CN: 「今天是难得的休息日。钟表应该配合我才对。」
en: “It’s a rare day off. The clock ought to work around me.”

zh_CN: 「医院里可从没听你这么说过。」
en: “I’ve never heard you say that at the hospital.”

zh_CN: 「医院里哪能这么说。七点该接患者，就是七点。手术器械少了一把，难道还能说等我睡醒再找吗？」
en: “How could I? If a patient is due at seven, it means seven. If an instrument is missing, can I say I’ll look for it after I’ve had my sleep?”

zh_CN: 「所以只要一下班，你就完全换了个人？」
en: “So the moment you finish work, you become a completely different person?”

zh_CN: 「也不是换了个人。就是这个人才终于可以偷懒了。」
en: “Not a different person. This person finally gets to be lazy.”

zh_CN: 朝仓点了一份热三明治，又认真研究起甜点栏。
en: Asakura orders a hot sandwich, then studies the dessert section intently.

zh_CN: 「你不是说要吃饭吗？怎么还在看蛋糕？」
en: “Didn’t you say you needed a meal? Why are you still looking at cake?”

zh_CN: 「饭是现在吃的。蛋糕是饭后吃的。医生应该懂顺序吧？」
en: “The meal is for now. The cake is for afterward. Surely a doctor understands the order?”

zh_CN: 「我还以为你有什么特别的饮食计划。」
en: “I thought you might have some special diet plan.”

zh_CN: 「有啊。第一步，先把饿了半天的自己喂饱。」
en: “I do. Step one: feed the me who’s been hungry for half a day.”

zh_CN: 「第二步呢？」
en: “And step two?”

zh_CN: 「让陪我等了一个小时的帅医生，也吃得开心一点。」
en: “Make sure the handsome doctor who waited an hour for me enjoys his meal too.”

zh_CN: 「……你这是在哄我？」
en: “…Are you trying to sweet-talk me?”

zh_CN: 「不行吗？平时我哄患者可熟练了。」
en: “Can’t I? I’m very good at reassuring patients.”

zh_CN: 「所以我今天是患者？」
en: “So I’m a patient today?”

zh_CN: 「如果你愿意的话，我可以负责把你照顾到心情变好哦。」
en: “If you’d like, I could take care of you until you feel better.”

zh_CN: 「总觉得听起来有哪里不对。」
en: “Something about that doesn’t sound quite right.”

zh_CN: 「呵呵。那就先吃饭，不聊医院啦。」
en: “Hehe. Let’s eat first, then. No more hospital talk.”

zh_CN: 热三明治端上桌。朝仓咬下第一口，满足地闭起眼睛，刚才所有的机灵话似乎都暂时被食物打败了。
en: The hot sandwich arrives. Asakura closes her eyes in satisfaction at the first bite, all her clever remarks momentarily defeated by food.

zh_CN: 「好吃吗？」
en: “Good?”

zh_CN: 「嗯！你尝尝。这个酱汁很好吃。」
en: “Mm! Try some. This sauce is delicious.”

zh_CN: 「你明明迟到了，现在倒像在带我探店。」
en: “You were late, but now you sound like you’re showing me your favorite places.”

zh_CN: 「那当然。迟到了就更要让剩下的时间过得值嘛。」
en: “Of course. Being late means I have to make the rest of our time even more worthwhile.”

zh_CN: 吃完饭，窗外的阳光斜斜地照在桌上。朝仓用小勺敲了敲甜点杯，终于不再急着说话。
en: After they eat, sunlight slants across the table. Asakura taps her dessert glass with a small spoon and finally stops rushing to speak.

zh_CN: 「你在医院做事的时候，真不像刚来的新人。」
en: “When I watch you work, you really don’t seem like a newcomer.”

zh_CN: 「又来了。上次不是跟你说过，我只是刚来星见吗？」
en: “This again? Didn’t I tell you last time that I’m only new to Hoshimi?”

zh_CN: 「我是说，你对交班、手术室的习惯，还有新人会在哪一步出错，好像都很清楚。」
en: “I mean, you seem to know all about handovers, operating-room routines, and exactly where newcomers will make mistakes.”

zh_CN: 「嗯……因为以前也做过这些呀。」
en: “Well… I’ve done all those things before.”

zh_CN: 「你以前到底负责过多少事？」
en: “Just how much were you responsible for?”

zh_CN: 「普通护理、排班、带新人……后来还当过第二护理班的班长。」
en: “Routine nursing, scheduling, training new staff… Later I was even the leader of the second nursing team.”

zh_CN: 「班长？」
en: “Team leader?”

zh_CN: 「正式的哦。带着一群人上班，下班前还得确认大家有没有把事情交清楚。」
en: “Officially. I led a whole team on shift, and before leaving I had to make sure everyone had handed everything over properly.”

zh_CN: 「那你怎么来星见以后，一直说自己是没经验的新护士？」
en: “Then why have you kept calling yourself an inexperienced new nurse since coming to Hoshimi?”

zh_CN: 「因为这里的制度和人，我的确不熟悉呀。旧医院怎么排班，不代表星见也照着做。」
en: “Because I really am unfamiliar with the people and systems here. The way my old hospital scheduled things doesn’t mean Hoshimi does the same.”

zh_CN: 「听起来倒很严谨。」
en: “That sounds quite conscientious.”

zh_CN: 「你要是以为我会因此变得老老实实，那可就错了。」
en: “If you think that means I’m going to become meek and obedient, you’re wrong.”

zh_CN: 「现在已经不敢这么想了。」
en: “I wouldn’t dare think that now.”

zh_CN: 「以前升上去的时候，大家都说是好事。能管更多人，讲话也更有分量。」
en: “When I was promoted, everyone said it was a good thing. I could manage more people, and my words carried more weight.”

zh_CN: 「最开始我也挺高兴的。谁不喜欢自己的工作被认可呢？」
en: “At first, I was happy too. Who doesn’t like having their work recognized?”

zh_CN: 「后来呢？」
en: “And then?”

zh_CN: 「后来发现，每个人都希望你站在自己那一边。」
en: “Then I found that everyone wanted me on their side.”

zh_CN: 「明明是为了给患者安排护理，最后却变成要先猜哪位上级会不会不高兴。」
en: “What should have been arranging nursing care for patients turned into guessing which superior might be upset first.”

zh_CN: 「你不喜欢那种工作？」
en: “You didn’t like that kind of work?”

zh_CN: 「我不讨厌管事。有人忙不过来，谁该去帮；新人跟不上，怎样教到她会——这些我都喜欢。」
en: “I don’t mind managing things. Who should help when someone is overwhelmed; how to teach a newcomer until she understands—I like all that.”

zh_CN: 「可是替人赔笑、打听谁跟谁有矛盾、替上面的人收拾不是护理工作的烂摊子……那就算了吧。」
en: “But smiling to appease people, finding out who’s fighting with whom, cleaning up messes for the higher-ups that have nothing to do with nursing… No, thank you.”

zh_CN: 「你以前也会直接这么说？」
en: “Did you say that outright back then too?”

zh_CN: 「会呀。只不过说了以后，总有人觉得我不懂事。」
en: “Yes. Though whenever I did, someone would say I was immature.”

zh_CN: 「你现在看起来倒不像会在意。」
en: “You don’t look as though that would bother you now.”

zh_CN: 「我会在意哦。只是有一天突然觉得，为什么非要让那些人决定我每天开不开心？」
en: “It does. But one day I suddenly thought: why should those people get to decide whether I’m happy every day?”

zh_CN: 朝仓舀起一小口甜点，像是在谈论一件已经想得很清楚的事情。
en: Asakura scoops up a small spoonful of dessert, as though discussing something she has already thought through thoroughly.

zh_CN: 「我想照顾患者，也想教新人。这些事情有意思，我就继续做。」
en: “I want to care for patients and teach newcomers. Those things interest me, so I’ll keep doing them.”

zh_CN: 「不想整天站队，也不想每天下班还去陪我讨厌的人吃饭。那我就不要再当那种班长了。」
en: “I don’t want to take sides all day, or have dinner with people I dislike every evening after work. So I won’t be that kind of team leader anymore.”

zh_CN: 「所以来星见，是你自己选的？」
en: “So coming to Hoshimi was your own choice?”

zh_CN: 「当然。你不会以为是我在旧医院什么都做不好，才来这里重新培训吧？」
en: “Of course. You didn’t think I came here for retraining because I couldn’t do anything right at my old hospital, did you?”

zh_CN: 「我可没这么说。」
en: “I never said that.”

zh_CN: 「那就好。要不然明天我可得重新检查一下你的交班表。」
en: “Good. Otherwise I might have to check your handover sheet again tomorrow.”

zh_CN: 「喂，今天不是不聊工作吗？」
en: “Hey, weren’t we avoiding work talk today?”

zh_CN: 「对哦。差点又把医院带到约会里了。」
en: “Oh, right. I nearly brought the hospital into our date again.”

zh_CN: 「不过你现在真的挺开心的。」
en: “But you really do seem happy now.”

zh_CN: 「嗯。可以认真工作，可以睡懒觉，可以追电视剧，也可以穿漂亮衣服出来吃好吃的。」
en: “I am. I can work hard, sleep in, watch dramas, and dress up to go out for good food.”

zh_CN: 「我才二十三岁呢。难道除了值班和排班，就没有别的事情值得期待吗？」
en: “I’m only twenty-three. Surely there’s more to look forward to than shifts and rotas?”

zh_CN: 「说得也是。那你接下来还想做什么？」
en: “Fair enough. What else would you like to do?”

zh_CN: 「好多呀。想去海边，想看新上映的电影，想睡到自然醒……」
en: “So much. Go to the seaside, see a new film, sleep until I wake up naturally…”

zh_CN: 「最后那个今天已经完成了吧。」
en: “You already managed the last one today.”

zh_CN: 「还想找个顺眼的男人，偶尔陪我出来约会。」
en: “And find a man I like the look of to take me on a date now and then.”

zh_CN: 「唔？反应这么平淡？」
en: “Hmm? Such a mild reaction?”

zh_CN: 「因为你说得太自然了。」
en: “You said it so naturally.”

zh_CN: 「本来就是很自然的事情嘛。」
en: “It is perfectly natural.”

zh_CN: 「与其去巴结那些讨厌的权势医生，我还不如调戏一下自己看得顺眼的帅医生呢。」
en: “Rather than flatter those awful, powerful doctors, I’d much rather tease a handsome doctor I actually like.”

zh_CN: 「……你说的那个医生，不会就是我吧？」
en: “…You wouldn’t happen to mean me, would you?”

zh_CN: 「呵呵。你觉得呢？」
en: “Hehe. What do you think?”

zh_CN: 她没急着接下一句话，只把勺子放回碟中，笑眯眯地看着坂口。
en: She doesn’t rush to say anything else, merely sets her spoon back on the saucer and smiles at Sakaguchi.

zh_CN: 「你一定是故意不说清楚。」
en: “You’re being deliberately vague.”

zh_CN: 「人家好不容易才约到你一天，当然得让今天有趣一点。」
en: “It took me so long to get a whole day with you. Of course I have to make it interesting.”

zh_CN: 「你不是在三点才想起来有这个约会吗？」
en: “Didn’t you only remember this date at three?”

zh_CN: 「……讨厌。这个笑话可以到此为止了吧？」
en: “…You’re awful. Can we retire that joke now?”

zh_CN: 「刚才是谁说要让今天有趣一点的？」
en: “Who just said she wanted to make today interesting?”

zh_CN: 「唔……看来坂口医生也不是完全不会还嘴。」
en: “Hmm… So Dr. Sakaguchi can talk back after all.”

zh_CN: 朝仓笑着伸手拿过账单。坂口还想说什么，她已经起身走向收银台。
en: Asakura smiles and reaches for the bill. Before Sakaguchi can say anything more, she is already on her way to the till.

zh_CN: 「走吧。下午还没过完呢。」
en: “Come on. The afternoon isn’t over yet.”

zh_CN: 离开餐厅，两人顺着商店街走到河边。临水的步道上吹着微风，周日的人群比店里少了许多。
en: Leaving the restaurant, they follow the shopping street to the river. A breeze blows along the waterside path, where the Sunday crowds are much thinner than in the shops.

zh_CN: 「你刚才说喜欢教新人。可有时候你对新人也挺严厉的。」
en: “You said you like teaching newcomers. But sometimes you’re quite strict with them.”

zh_CN: 「是吗？我还以为我在星见已经非常温柔了呢。」
en: “Am I? I thought I’d been exceptionally gentle here at Hoshimi.”

zh_CN: 「有时看着别人紧张，你似乎还有一点高兴。」
en: “Sometimes you even seem a little pleased to see someone nervous.”

zh_CN: 「被发现了？」
en: “You caught me?”

zh_CN: 「你承认得也太快了。」
en: “You admitted that far too quickly.”

zh_CN: 「紧张不一定是坏事呀。新人知道自己还有很多东西不懂，才会认真问我。」
en: “Being nervous isn’t always bad. Newcomers ask me serious questions because they know how much they don’t understand.”

zh_CN: 「患者也是。有人一边害怕，一边又特别想听接下来会发生什么。」
en: “Patients too. Some are scared, but still desperately want to hear what will happen next.”

zh_CN: 「……你说的是之前那位女警吗？」
en: “…Do you mean that policewoman from before?”

zh_CN: 「呵呵。不止她一个哦。」
en: “Hehe. She’s not the only one.”

zh_CN: 「你明明说今天不聊医院。」
en: “You said we wouldn’t talk about the hospital today.”

zh_CN: 「这是我的个人兴趣，不算讨论排班。两回事嘛。」
en: “This is a personal interest, not a discussion about the rota. Two different things.”

zh_CN: 「听起来有点危险。」
en: “That sounds a little dangerous.”

zh_CN: 「那我告诉你一件更危险的事？」
en: “Shall I tell you something even more dangerous?”

zh_CN: 「你先说说看。」
en: “Let’s hear it.”

zh_CN: 朝仓转过身，面对着坂口倒退了两步。她像是要说一个很正经的专业观点，忽然把声音压低。
en: Asakura turns to face Sakaguchi and takes two steps backward. As if about to offer a serious professional opinion, she suddenly lowers her voice.

zh_CN: 「我一直觉得，手术其实就像一场超大型的 SM Play。」
en: “I’ve always thought surgery is actually like an enormous SM play session.”

zh_CN: 「你想嘛。人在外面能走、能坐、能自己决定事情，进了手术室，就得把好多事交给医生和护士安排。」
en: “Think about it. Outside, people can walk, sit, and make their own decisions. Once they enter the operating room, so much has to be left to the doctors and nurses.”

zh_CN: 「……这倒是真的。」
en: “…That’s true.”

zh_CN: 「床上的位置、手脚怎么放、什么时候能动……明明是自己的身体，接下来的节奏却都得听我们的。」
en: “Where they lie, where their hands and feet go, when they can move… It’s their own body, but we set the pace for everything that follows.”

zh_CN: 「那是为了手术。」
en: “That’s for the operation.”

zh_CN: 「我知道呀。可是你不觉得，那种害怕、害羞，又不得不信任对方的感觉……很微妙吗？」
en: “I know. But don’t you think that mixture of fear, embarrassment, and having to trust someone else… is rather intriguing?”

zh_CN: 「我还是第一次听护士这样形容自己的工作。」
en: “I’ve never heard a nurse describe her work that way before.”

zh_CN: 「呵呵。那说明其他人比较会藏。」
en: “Hehe. That just means the others hide it better.”

zh_CN: 「你不会真的拿患者当成什么游戏对象吧？」
en: “You don’t actually treat patients as playthings, do you?”

zh_CN: 「工作的时候当然要做好工作。我又不会因为自己觉得有趣，就故意把手术弄乱。」
en: “Of course I do my job properly at work. I wouldn’t deliberately disrupt an operation just because I found something amusing.”

zh_CN: 「不过，观察患者的反应，本来就是护士的本事呀。明明怕得要命，还忍不住继续打听下一步，有时候真的很好懂。」
en: “But observing a patient’s reactions is part of a nurse’s skill. Terrified, yet unable to stop asking what comes next—sometimes they’re very easy to read.”

zh_CN: 「所以你就笑眯眯地等着她们继续问？」
en: “So you just smile and wait for them to keep asking?”

zh_CN: 「既然是她们自己想知道，我总不能抢着把答案塞过去嘛。」
en: “If they want to know, I can hardly rush to force the answers on them.”

zh_CN: 「……难怪那天你那么高兴。」
en: “…No wonder you were so pleased that day.”

zh_CN: 「不过，也不是每个患者都会有这种感觉。」
en: “Still, not every patient feels that way.”

zh_CN: 「我跟过那么多台手术，年轻女患者里面，那种又怕又好奇、总在意我们下一步会做什么的，倒还真不少。」
en: “In all the operations I’ve assisted with, quite a few young women have been both frightened and curious, always wondering what we’ll do next.”

zh_CN: 「年纪大一些的患者，好像就没那么明显了。」
en: “It doesn’t seem quite as obvious with older patients.”

zh_CN: 「……你观察得还真仔细。」
en: “…You really do pay close attention.”

zh_CN: 「毕竟我是护士嘛。看出患者究竟在担心什么，可是工作的一部分。」
en: “I am a nurse, after all. Working out what a patient is actually worried about is part of the job.”

zh_CN: 她说完便笑着转回身，随手拨开被风吹到脸侧的发丝。
en: She smiles and turns forward again, casually brushing the windblown hair away from her cheek.

zh_CN: 「不过说起来……我们医院不知道为什么，几乎都是年轻女患者呢。」
en: “Come to think of it… for some reason, almost all the patients at our hospital are young women.”

zh_CN: 「坂口医生，你不觉得有点奇怪吗？」
en: “Dr. Sakaguchi, don’t you think that’s a little strange?”

zh_CN: 「这个问题你问我，我也不知道怎么回答。」
en: “I wouldn’t know how to answer that even if you asked me.”

zh_CN: 「呵呵呵。真奇怪呢。」
en: “Hehehe. Very strange.”

zh_CN: 朝仓若无其事地继续往前走，只留下坂口站在原地思考自己究竟被问了什么。
en: Asakura walks on as though nothing happened, leaving Sakaguchi standing there wondering what exactly he has just been asked.

zh_CN: 天色渐渐柔和。两人在河边的长椅坐下，远处有人骑着自行车经过，车铃声很快消失在风里。
en: The light gradually softens. They sit on a bench beside the river. Someone cycles past in the distance, and the bell soon fades into the breeze.

zh_CN: 「不过我现在倒能理解，你为什么不想再管那些派系和职位了。」
en: “I can understand now why you don’t want to deal with factions and positions anymore.”

zh_CN: 「突然又这么认真？」
en: “So serious all of a sudden?”

zh_CN: 「你明明比很多人都擅长管理。可听你刚才说的，你好像很清楚自己不想要什么。」
en: “You’re clearly better at managing people than many others. But from what you’ve said, you seem to know exactly what you don’t want.”

zh_CN: 「这也是花了点时间才想明白的。」
en: “It took me some time to work that out.”

zh_CN: 「你跟芹香以前就在同一家医院吧？」
en: “You and Serika used to work at the same hospital, didn’t you?”
“…Yes.”

zh_CN: 「你们一起到星见，是不是发生过什么？」
en: “You came to Hoshimi together. Did something happen?”

zh_CN: 朝仓望着河面，手指慢慢收起身旁的小包带子。她没有立刻回答。
en: Asakura gazes at the river, slowly gathering up the strap of the small bag beside her. She doesn’t answer right away.

zh_CN: 「坂口医生。」
en: “Dr. Sakaguchi.”
“Yes?”

zh_CN: 「那边的事，就留在那边吧。」
en: “Let’s leave what happened there, there.”

zh_CN: 「……抱歉。我不该突然问。」
en: “…Sorry. I shouldn’t have asked so suddenly.”

zh_CN: 「不用道歉。我知道你是好奇。」
en: “You don’t need to apologize. I know you’re curious.”

zh_CN: 「只是，有些事情我现在还不想说。」
en: “There are just some things I don’t want to talk about yet.”

zh_CN: 她回过头，笑容依旧，只是这次没有故意逗他。
en: She turns back, still smiling, but this time she isn’t teasing him.

zh_CN: 「如果你想认识我的话……先认识现在的我，好不好？」
en: “If you want to get to know me… could you start with who I am now?”
“Of course.”

zh_CN: 「这么干脆？」
en: “That easily?”

zh_CN: 「你不想说，我就不问了。」
en: “If you don’t want to talk, I won’t ask.”
“…Thank you.”

zh_CN: 远处的河面映着夕阳。朝仓把视线移开了一会儿，随后像是想起什么，再次看向坂口。
en: The distant river reflects the sunset. Asakura looks away for a moment, then turns back to Sakaguchi as though something has occurred to her.

zh_CN: 「不过，有件事我想拜托你。」
en: “There is one thing I’d like to ask you, though.”

zh_CN: 「什么？」
en: “What is it?”

zh_CN: 「有空的话，多帮帮芹香，好吗？」
en: “When you can, would you help Serika a little more?”

zh_CN: 「芹香？」
en: “Serika?”

zh_CN: 「她有时候不太会把自己想说的话说出来。你跟她共事，应该也感觉到了吧。」
en: “Sometimes she struggles to say what she wants to say. You’ve probably noticed that working with her.”
“…A little.”

zh_CN: 「我不能替她说那些事。可是，如果她有一天愿意自己告诉你……你就听她说，好吗？」
en: “I can’t tell you those things for her. But if one day she wants to tell you herself… would you hear her out?”

zh_CN: 「嗯。我记住了。」
en: “Yes. I’ll remember.”

zh_CN: 「那就拜托你啦。」
en: “Then I’m counting on you.”

zh_CN: 她轻轻呼出一口气，像是终于把一件惦记着的小事交代妥当。
en: She exhales softly, as though she has finally entrusted him with a small concern that has been on her mind.

zh_CN: 「好——！今天的认真话题结束！」
en: “All right—! That’s enough serious talk for today!”

zh_CN: 「切换得真快。」
en: “You switch gears quickly.”

zh_CN: 「难得出来约会，我才不要从头到尾都像在开护理会议。」
en: “It’s a rare chance to go on a date. I don’t want the whole thing to feel like a nursing meeting.”

zh_CN: 「那你接下来想做什么？」
en: “What would you like to do next?”

zh_CN: 「嗯……先去看一眼那边的甜品店有没有关门。」
en: “Hmm… First, let’s see if that dessert shop is still open.”

zh_CN: 「你刚才不是吃过蛋糕了吗？」
en: “Didn’t you just have cake?”

zh_CN: 「那个是下午茶。现在已经快到晚饭时间了呀。」
en: “That was afternoon tea. It’s almost dinnertime now.”

zh_CN: 「你的时间观念还真是随心所欲。」
en: “Your sense of time really does follow its own rules.”

zh_CN: 「医院里的时间是给患者和大家的。今天剩下的时间，我想留给自己。」
en: “At the hospital, my time belongs to the patients and everyone else. I want to keep the rest of today for myself.”
“…Fair enough.”

zh_CN: 「还有你。」
en: “And you.”
“Huh?”

zh_CN: 「不然我今天为什么这么急着赶来？难道只为了一个人吃三明治吗？」
en: “Why else would I have rushed over today? Just to eat a sandwich on my own?”

zh_CN: 「这话说得倒像你没迟到一样。」
en: “You make it sound as if you weren’t late.”

zh_CN: 「哎呀。坂口君，今天可以暂时不提这件事了吗？」
en: “Oh, Sakaguchi-kun. Could we stop bringing that up for the rest of today?”

zh_CN: 那声「坂口君」说得轻快自然。坂口刚转头，朝仓已经站起身，向他伸出手。
en: Her “Sakaguchi-kun” comes lightly and naturally. As Sakaguchi turns, Asakura is already standing, holding out her hand.

zh_CN: 「……好吧。今天就放过你。」
en: “…All right. I’ll let you off today.”

zh_CN: 「呵呵。果然是个好医生。」
en: “Hehe. You really are a good doctor.”

zh_CN: 「这跟医生有什么关系？」
en: “What does being a doctor have to do with it?”

zh_CN: 「肯等我，肯听我说话，还肯陪我去吃第二顿点心。评价很高哦。」
en: “You waited for me, listened to me, and will even join me for a second round of dessert. Very high marks.”

zh_CN: 「你的评价标准还挺奇怪。」
en: “You have some strange criteria.”

zh_CN: 「你今天才知道？」
en: “You only just noticed?”

zh_CN: 坂口握住她伸来的手，两人沿着亮起路灯的步道往商店街走去。
en: Sakaguchi takes her outstretched hand, and they walk along the path toward the shopping street as the streetlights come on.

zh_CN: 「对了，下次约会我一定准时。」
en: “Oh, and I’ll definitely be on time for our next date.”

zh_CN: 「你打算几点设闹钟？」
en: “What time will you set your alarm?”

zh_CN: 「……不如你打电话叫我起床吧？」
en: “…Why don’t you call to wake me up?”

zh_CN: 「那不就跟今天一样吗？」
en: “Wouldn’t that be just like today?”

zh_CN: 「不一样呀。今天是三点才听到你的早安。」
en: “It’s different. Today I didn’t hear your good morning until three.”

zh_CN: 「下次……我想早点听到。」
en: “Next time… I’d like to hear it earlier.”

zh_CN: 她说完笑了笑，手却没有松开。远处的店铺橱窗亮起温暖的灯光。
en: She smiles, but doesn’t let go of his hand. Warm lights come on in the shop windows ahead.
